sections.heading: Idioms with body parts
sections.body:
- *no tener ni pies ni cabeza* — to make no sense at all
- *hablar por los codos* — to talk nonstop
- *tener mala leche* — to be mean / have bad luck (varies by country; in Mexico *mala leche* = bad luck or bad intentions)
- *echar(le) el ojo a algo* — to have your eye on something
- *con el corazón en la mano* — sincerely, openly
- *poner el grito en el cielo* — to hit the roof, protest loudly
- *estar con el agua al cuello* — to be up to your neck (in trouble / debt)
- *costar sangre, sudor y lágrimas* — to take blood, sweat and tears

sections.heading: Proverbs (refranes)
sections.body:
Proverbs are used a lot in everyday conversation, often just the first half:

- *Más vale tarde que nunca.* — Better late than never.
- *En boca cerrada no entran moscas.* — Silence is golden (lit. flies don't enter a closed mouth).
- *Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.* — You snooze, you lose (lit. the shrimp that falls asleep is carried off by the current). Very Latin American.
- *Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.* — A man is known by the company he keeps.
- *No hay mal que por bien no venga.* — Every cloud has a silver lining.
- *Más vale pájaro en mano que cien volando.* — A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
- *A caballo regalado no se le mira el diente.* — Don't look a gift horse in the mouth.
- *Del dicho al hecho hay mucho trecho.* — Easier said than done.
